source.citation: Briones, J. C. A., Papa, R. D. S., Cauyan, G. A., Mendoza, N., & Okuda, N. (2016). Fish diversity and trophic interactions in Lake Sampaloc (Luzon Is., Philippines). Tropical Ecology, 57(3), 567-581.
source.access: The complete article text was visible on a public ResearchGate page identifying the paper as author-uploaded by Jonathan Carlo Briones on 2026-01-21. The UST author profile independently confirms the journal citation. The cited publisher archive URL was not accessible in this review. No local PDF was retained.
source.copyright: The article front matter states © International Society for Tropical Ecology (2016). ResearchGate says content may be subject to copyright. No open license or item-specific reuse grant was found.

studyScope.samplingEffort: The methods describe monthly rapid surveys with local fishermen, two gill nets with 15 mm and 35 mm mesh, and 11 survey trips in total. Specimens were photographed, identified, and measured.
studyScope.trophicSampling: Stable-isotope samples were collected in October 2013 from fish and potential food items including leaf litter, periphyton, phytoplankton, and zooplankton.
sourceBoundaries: Historical site-specific study; does not establish current presence or a present-day whole-lake checklist.
It covers Lake Sampaloc, not the other six San Pablo lakes.
The paper's Table 1 is a provisional checklist, but its cells were not transcribed into this review because item-specific reuse permission is unresolved.
No coordinate, waterbody geometry, population estimate, catchability, legal status, access, safety, or abundance claim was added.

trophicEvidence.sourceReportedFinding: The authors infer from their October 2013 stable-isotope analysis that tilapine cichlids, including Nile tilapia and red tilapia, primarily grazed or exploited littoral periphyton in Lake Sampaloc; other fish may have depended indirectly on prey supported by periphyton production.
trophicEvidence.locator: Tropical Ecology 57(3), discussion, journal page 576; web-extracted article lines 1721-1732.
trophicEvidence.interpretation: This is a historical, site-specific trophic-production finding, not an exhaustive stomach-content diet, a national species-level diet profile, or a bait recommendation. Do not generalize it to all tilapia populations or current lake conditions. No diet claim was admitted to the app.

relationshipToSevenLakesConflict.interpretation: This separate Lake Sampaloc study cannot resolve the Bunot Lake Carassius identity conflict. Its article checklist is not transcribed here; no per-lake record was inferred from the other Seven Lakes study.

nextAction: Seek item-specific reuse terms or an independently reusable dataset if considering a Lake Sampaloc species/diet projection. If used for the diet feature, preserve the source, lake, 2013 sampling context, trophic-method qualifier, and distinction from bait advice.
